core_obligations: Let k-bar be a separable algebraic closure of k and use finiteness of the irreducible components of X together with the orbit statement to conclude that X over the closure has finitely many irreducible components (proof lines 1858-1863).
Apply the definability statement to descend all of those finitely many components to irreducible components over one finite extension k' of k (proof lines 1863-1867).

Read off the conclusion: every irreducible component of X_{k'} is geometrically irreducible over k', since its base change to the closure is one of the listed components and irreducible spaces are nonempty by definition (proof line 1867).
proof_roadmap: Finitely many components over the closure (proof lines 1858-1863).
Common finite extension by definability (proof lines 1863-1867).
difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over k with finitely many irreducible components, the lemma produces a finite separable extension k'/k such that every irreducible component of X_{k'} is geometrically irreducible over k' (statement lines 1847-1855). The proof descends the finiteness of the set of components to the separable closure using the Galois orbit statement for components, so that the components over the closure form a finite list, and then applies the definability statement for components of the base change to descend each of them to a common finite extension (proof lines 1858-1867). The claim is H2: two parts of a single cited lemma combined with the finiteness hypothesis, with the common finite extension for all components as the point of the argument.
